sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1986), supplemented by the Investment Protocol of 2009
Free Trade Agreement between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China (signed 2013, entered into force 1 July 2014)
Convention between the Swiss Confederation and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Switzerland-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1971, as amended by the 2010 Additional Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act of 10 October 1997 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (GwG/AMLA; SR 955.0), as amended; Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV; SR 955.01); FINMA Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (GwV-FINMA; SR 955.04); Swiss Criminal Code (StGB; SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR; SR 220); Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV; SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Enforcement of International Sanctions (Embargo Act; SR 946.231). Switzerland does not operate a publicly searchable beneficial-owner register; UBO records are maintained internally by financial intermediaries, fiduciaries, and legal professionals subject to AMLA, and are disclosed to competent authorities where legal obligations require.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport or national identity document of each beneficial owner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/identity authority in the country of origin or foreign consular/notarial authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention, consular legalization through the competent Swiss Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certified commercial register excerpt for every corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial registrar or company registry in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; otherwise consular legalization by Swiss diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address of each beneficial owner (utility bill or recent bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or issuing utility/financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on notarized certification; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution confirming the client's business profile and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The issuing bank or regulated financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the bank refuses a notarized signature; otherwise bank-stamped original

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no tax arrears or tax residence certificate for each controlling beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National or cantonal tax administration in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; otherwise consular legalization through Swiss representation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Swiss SECO Economic Sanctions lists, European Union sanctions where implemented by Switzerland, and OFAC SDN lists as a cross-border USD-payment benchmark. PEP status must be identified through commercial PEP databases and confirmed by self-declaration; PEPs require enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Negative news and financial-integrity checks must be documented in the KYC file. KYC records must be retained for at least ten years after the business relationship ends, in accordance with AMLA record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Name Index) at www.zefix.ch, operated in conjunction with the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce; formal applications are filed through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names (Firmen) must be permissible in an official Swiss language and use the Latin alphabet. Where a proposed commercial name is in a language other than German, French, Italian, or Romansh, it must be transliterated into a Swiss official language. The legal form must be expressed in the language of the registered office: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' in German, 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' in French, and 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' in Italian. Names must not contain misleading statements and must comply with Swiss regulations on commercial names under Articles 927-940 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal Commercial Register Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its notary may first request a written reasoning. A corrected new application may be submitted after removing the prohibited or confusing element. If the registrar confirms legal impediments, the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days of receipt of the written rejection to the competent cantonal administrative authority or administrative court, in accordance with cantonal administrative procedure. A further appeal to the Federal Administrative Court is available where federal law issues arise. Extensions of a preliminary name availability confirmation are possible by written application before expiry only if no conflicting name has been registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or service-based registered office is permissible for this low-risk online consumer-electronics retail activity only if a physical Swiss office is maintained by a professional corporate-services, fiduciary, or law firm that accepts service of legal process, retains correspondence, and is registered at a genuine street address in the canton. A P.O. Box alone, a remote online mailbox, or a purely virtual address without an authorized Swiss representative does not satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement under Swiss company law. The company must maintain its seat and practical administration in Switzerland to retain Swiss tax residence unless a treaty-based or permanent-establishment analysis is otherwise documented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk for an ISIC 4791 online retail company is low, estimated at under 2% per annum for unannounced physical on-site inspections. The commercial register office, cantonal tax administration, and AML supervisory bodies may conduct targeted inspections if anomalies arise in tax filings, de-registration, or payment-rail due diligence; the probability increases materially if the company uses high-risk payment flows or non-resident UBO structures. A standard registered-office inspection would be a scheduled visit, not an unannounced raid.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal preliminary company-name availability query and name-clearance processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the cantonal commercial register fee ordinance, approximately CHF 100-150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the articles of association and foundation declaration by a Swiss public notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss public notary in the canton of registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal notarial fee schedule, generally CHF 1,500-2,500 depending on share capital and complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing and entry of Aktiengesellschaft in the Swiss Commercial Register, including publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Federal Official Gazette Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and publication tariffs under the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance and SOGC fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank confirmation on paid-up share capital deposit and escrow/blocked-account certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank or FINMA-regulated financial institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark bank fee for blocked-account confirmation under Article 633 of the Swiss Code of Obligations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML/KYC file preparation, beneficial-owner analysis, PEP screening, and sanctions-list checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss fiduciary, corporate-services provider, or independent AML compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for standard AMLA-compliant onboarding due diligence of a low-risk AG

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular-legalization bundle for up to five foreign-origin due-diligence documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent apostille authorities, Swiss embassies/consulates, or authorized legalization agents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government statutory per-document fees plus agent service fee, approximately $50-$90 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Swiss-language translation of foreign shareholders' documentation and corporate-account filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized certified translation bureau or notarially certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-page translation and certification fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year Swiss registered-office and commercial-substance service fee, including handling of official mail and tax correspondence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary or corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual registered-office fee for a small e-commerce AG, typically CHF 2,000-3,000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Articles 620 to 763 concerning the Aktiengesellschaft (AG); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung) and Federal Act on Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (Errichtungserklärung / acte constitutif) together with the articles of association (Statuten / status), submitted electronically to the Commercial Register Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An AG must have nominal share capital of at least CHF 100,000. At least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash before registration, evidenced by a blocked-account confirmation issued by a Swiss bank; the capital remains escrowed until the company is entered in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the statutory first meeting of the Board of Directors: (1) The founders' subscription of 100 registered shares at CHF 1,000 each, forming share capital of CHF 100,000, is approved and ratified. (2) The paid-up amount of CHF 50,000, held on blocked account, is confirmed and accepted as available to the company upon entry in the Commercial Register. (3) The registered office is fixed at [street, Zug, Switzerland]. (4) The following officers are appointed: [Name], Chairman; [Name], member; signature rules are fixed. (5) The annual audit is waived under article 727a OR. (6) The notary and counsel are directed to file this resolution with the Commercial Register and SHAB.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company-name availability verification and constitutional document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ZEFIX central business name index and preliminary confirmation from Handelsregisteramt Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the desired exact company name on zefix.ch to verify availability, linguistic neutrality, and absence of confusingly similar names. Then instruct a Swiss notary to prepare German-language articles of association reflecting the AG share capital, registered office, purpose, board composition, and audit opt-out.
required_dossiers: Declaration of the intended Swiss registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects that the name is identical or misleading, submit an alternative name through the notary or file a written objection under the Commercial Register Ordinance; cure within the registry's deadline of usually 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocked capital deposit account and obtaining paid-in-capital confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank in Canton Zug (private or cantonal bank) with anti-money-laundering KYC acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders open a non-interest-bearing blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company in formation. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 representing the paid-up minimum. The bank issues a written blocked-account confirmation stating that funds are irrevocably earmarked and will be released only upon registration or as legally ordered.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association with share-capital clause
Bank account-opening mandate and beneficial-ownership identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional evidence on beneficial ownership or source of wealth, provide a Swiss-compliant enhanced due-diligence file. If the bank declines on compliance grounds, select another licensed bank and obtain a fresh blocked-account certificate before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public admitted in the Canton of Zug (öffentliche Beurkundung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear before the notary in person, identify themselves, and confirm the incorporation deed. The notary verifies the capital deposit confirmation, reads and explains the articles, and notarizes the deed and statutes. The notarial act also records the first board composition and the valid exercise of the audit waiver.
required_dossiers: Blocked-account capital confirmation from the Swiss bank
Founders' valid passports or Swiss identity cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a formal deficiency, amend the deed by an auxiliary notarial act before filing. If a foreign founder lacks capacity to appear, obtain an apostilled and legalized power of attorney naming a local signatory.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and approval of the pro-forma governance resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the newly incorporated Aktiengesellschaft, with minutes signed by the chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately following notarization, the board convenes and passes the first written resolution covering share subscription ratification, registered-office adoption, director and officer appointments, signature regulations, audit waiver, and authorization of the Commercial Register filing. The signed resolution is attached to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Accepted officer declarations and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director appointment is invalid or a director resigns before filing, the remaining directors may adopt a circular resolution replacing the appointee and supply a supplementary notice to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register filing and SHAB publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt Zug through the notary using the cantonal commercial-register electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the notarized deed, articles, first board resolution, officer signatures, and capital confirmation to the Commercial Register Office. The registry examines compliance with the Code of Obligations, enters the AG in the Commercial Register, assigns the register number and legal personality date, and causes publication in SHAB.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or interlocutory decision, the notary submits a corrective filing within the set deadline. A denial may be appealed to the Cantonal Administrative Court of Zug under cantonal and federal administrative procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration UID, tax, social-insurance and employer housekeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA), Zug Cantonal Tax Administration, and the AHV/AVS compensation fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Federal Business Identification Number (UID) automatically after commercial-register entry. Register for VAT through the FTA if taxable supplies from consumer-electronics online retail are expected to exceed CHF 100,000 annually. Register as an employer with the compensation fund for payroll and social-security contributions, confirm UID at the Zug tax office, and verify that no sector-specific retail license is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UID issuance or VAT registration is delayed, the responsible officer follows up directly with the FTA and commercial register, submitting the register excerpt and a short business description. Any request for further information should be answered within 30 days to avoid deemed refusal and possible penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies because the activity is pure online retail of consumer electronics and smart gadgets. For office and storage premises in Zug, the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate and the municipal building authority are the only relevant administrative bodies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required. The activity falls under general freedom of commerce under Article 27 of the Swiss Federal Constitution; no manufacturing, industrial, or special trading permit is issued for this ISIC 4791 retail scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and Cantonal Office for the Environment of Zug (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - e-commerce retail is not an installation listed in the Annex to the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/UEIA); no full EIA or preliminary scoping is required unless a future logistics warehouse crosses annex thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, stack emissions, or VOC-generating production exist. Compliance applies to waste handling under the Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VeVA), take-back and disposal obligations for waste electrical and electronic equipment under OREA/REGEL, and battery disposal under the Swiss Batteries Ordinance (OAB).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification must be confirmed for office and storage areas by the municipal fire-prevention authority of Zug, including structural-load clearance for shelving and racking. Workplace safety obligations apply under Article 82 of the Swiss Labour Act and Suva accident-prevention instructions; no special civil-defense permit is required for low-risk retail operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV), Main Division for Value Added Tax; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT e-filing portal: SukRe (www.sukre.admin.ch); Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix) and UID register managed by the Federal Statistical Office (www.uid.admin.ch). Cantonal tax authorities remain competent for profit/capital tax collection.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Switzerland that carries out taxable supplies in Switzerland exceeding CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover must obtain a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and register for VAT. Procedure: (1) apply for a UID via the FTA SukRe e-portal or the UID register, submitting certified constitutional documentation, power of attorney, and identification of beneficial owners; (2) file VAT registration form (e-form 0301) with the FTA Main Division for VAT, declaring the intended start date of taxable activity; (3) a non-resident entity without a Swiss branch must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (art. 67 VAT Act) who is jointly and severally liable for VAT; (4) upon approval, the FTA issues a VAT registration confirmation and the UID is extended with the suffix '-MWST' (e.g., CHE-000.000.000-MWST), which serves as the VAT identification number; (5) the entity must file quarterly or semi-annual VAT returns electronically through SukRe and maintain Swiss accounting records. Registration becomes effective from the commencement of taxable activity, and failure to register exposes the entity to assessment plus penalties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a US-style check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for foreign entities; an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is mandatorily taxed at the entity level. Available statutory elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration under art. 11 VAT Act where turnover is below the CHF 100,000 threshold; (ii) election to form a VAT group (art. 11 VAT Act) for closely held Swiss and foreign entities; (iii) option to tax real property under art. 22 VAT Act; (iv) tax-group election for direct federal tax purposes (art. 60-61 Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax) allowing domestic group members to be treated as a single taxpayer; (v) participation relief election under arts. 69-70 of the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax; (vi) recognition of a foreign entity's classification is governed exclusively by Swiss domestic tax law and DTT tie-breaker rules; the US 'check-the-box' election is not automatically recognized but may be relevant for US-Swiss treaty application. No hybrid-mismatch elections are available to AG shareholders under Swiss law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover (art. 10 para. 2 lit. a VAT Act). A foreign entity with turnover below the threshold may be exempt from registration, but a Swiss permanent establishment or a foreign entity supplying goods stored in Switzerland to Swiss consumers may nonetheless create a nexus. Voluntary registration is available under art. 11 VAT Act for corporations, cooperatives, foundations and Swiss permanent establishments of foreign businesses even if turnover does not reach CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime in Switzerland. E-invoicing is voluntary for B2B and B2C transactions; the Swiss QR-bill and the eBill infrastructure are widely used commercial standards. From 1 January 2026, suppliers to Swiss federal public authorities must issue e-invoices in Peppol BIS 3.0 format via an approved access point. VAT returns and ancillary declarations must be filed electronically through the FTA SukRe portal using XML/Web-service API interfaces; a PDF-only submission is tolerated only for micro taxpayers. There is no digital stamping, tax authority pre-clearance, or unique transaction code requirement for invoices in the private sector.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods is zero-rated with full input VAT deduction if the goods are physically dispatched or transported abroad within the statutory documentary framework (art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act). For online retail of consumer electronics, zero-rating applies where the retail sale is made to a foreign purchaser and the goods are exported from Switzerland (or from a Swiss customs warehouse) to a foreign destination. Directly related services (transport, handling, insurance costs) are also zero-rated. Services supplied to recipients with a business seat abroad are zero-rated where the service is provided to the foreign recipient (art. 23 para. 2 VAT Act). The seller must substantiate the export with a customs export declaration and transport evidence; missing proof causes the supply to be taxable at 8.1%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss e-dec / NCTS export declaration with customs clearance certificate)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (carrier-issued transport document evidencing movement out of Switzerland)
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT/MT103 or bank statement proving receipt of payment in foreign currency from the foreign buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims are vigorously pursued by the FTA. Under arts. 72 and 73 VAT Act, intentional tax evasion (including false export documentation or fictitious exports) is punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; negligent under-declaration attracts a fine of up to twice the tax; minor procedural infringements are fined up to CHF 8,000. The FTA may issue a discriminatory surcharge and publicly announce the penalty. There is a 10-year absolute limitation period and a 5-year relative limitation period for reassessment of undisclosed or misdeclared exports (art. 39 VAT Act). If the export proof bundle is incomplete or the inward remittance fails, the FTA retrospectively claws back the zero-rated treatment, imposes 8.1% VAT plus default interest, and may exclude the taxpayer from simplified export procedures and the status of approved economic operator.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank, with external exchange controls administered jointly with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for sanctions and due diligence matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no Swiss exchange control laws, no restriction on the repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds, and no authorization requirement for the acquisition of CHF by residents or non-residents. Switzerland operates a free capital market regime under the Federal Law on the Free Movement of Capital and the Bilateral Agreements with the EU, subject only to general anti-money laundering and sanctions screening. For an e-commerce retail entity, no prior governmental approval is required for cross-border payments, profit transfers, or dividend distribution, provided corporate vehicles are validly incorporated and tax obligations are settled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist in Switzerland. Export receipts in CHF or foreign currencies may be retained, settled, or converted freely. There is no minimum holding period and no requirement to repatriate export proceeds. A Swiss AG may maintain foreign currency accounts without restriction, and the SNB imposes no mandatory conversion ratio. For customs and VAT purposes, statutory record-keeping of export invoices and payment evidence is required for exemption claims, but no monetary surrender obligation applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_controls_summary: No restrictions on inbound or outbound portfolio or direct investments, including the issuance of shares to non-residents. Foreign investors do not require SNB or FINMA approval to hold shares in a Swiss AG, except for specific licensed activities (e.g., banking, insurance) not relevant to consumer electronics retail. Participation in the Swiss Guardian framework (Die Postfinance / Swiss Bankers Association) applies to sanctioned counterparties and beneficial ownership disclosure, but not to convertibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account in CHF and major FX) / Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account for Swiss-resident entities
Operational Account (best for e-commerce and low-risk retail)
Operational Account / Wealth-linked Escrow for high-value treasury

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (integrated into UBS Switzerland as of 2024)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Legacy operational account – not available for new onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately feasible, subject to FINMA FinTech licensing or a full banking license. Swiss law does not ‘passport’ foreign e-money institutions (EMIs) into Switzerland. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., UK or EU authorized) may hold an account with a Swiss bank only as a payment service provider, but cannot independently provide a Swiss IBAN or act as a full banking counterparty for a Swiss AG without establishing a Swiss branch or acquiring a FinTech license (deposit ceiling of CHF 100 million for public deposits). For clearing rail purposes, a Swiss-registered payment institution (e.g., a FINMA-licensed Fintech) can be used for e-commerce payouts (Stripe, PayPal) but is not a replacement for a corporate account at a tier-1 commercial bank. Feasibility rating: Medium for an EMI as an auxiliary clearing node; High for a Swiss bank relationship combined with a payment service provider.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted under Swiss banking practice provided the beneficial owners are natural persons physically identified either by remote video identification (with certified biometric / e-ID) or through a Swiss notary or foreign bank/embassy confirmation. For a Swiss AG with exclusively non-resident directors, most tier-1 banks (e.g., UBS, ZKB) require at least one face-to-face interview with the beneficial owner or a senior director at a bank branch or a Swiss notary public, especially when the beneficial owner holds >25% of shares. Physical presence is not a statutory mandate under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) if a qualified third party (bank, notary, or external audit firm) performs the identification according to FINMA Circular 2024/1. For practical onboarding success, recommend a single physical visit to the chosen bank for the UBO at stage 4. Alternative: use remote video in combination with a hard-to-forge E-ID for a minority of banks (e.g., Banca Migros SA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk e-commerce exposure: online payment acceptance, chargebacks, multiple refund flows, or direct-to-consumer geographies in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Detailed business plan and product catalogue (ISIC 4791 – consumer electronics); 2) clear refund and chargeback policy; 3) list of target jurisdictions and screening report excluding sanctioned entities; 4) payment processor MLRO confirmation; 5) transaction monitoring and sanctions filtering by Stripe/PayPal or an in-house screening tool; 6) cluster analysis showing average transaction size < CHF 1,000 and low fraud ratio; 7) strong KYC on marketplace sellers if it sub-licenses as a marketplace, not a pure principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director/shareholder with >25% ownership in a Swiss AG, especially if originating from a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Certified passport copy and proof of address (<3 months) for all UBOs; 2) clear organizational chart with UBO declaration per AMLA Art. 4; 3) tax residency certificate for UBO and source of wealth (sale agreement of assets, bank statement of initial capital); 4) notarised authorisation on non-executive board and confirmation that the AG has a Swiss domicile; 5) external audit confirmation for the first year if assets exceed CHF 1M; 6) no prior adverse corporate record and UBO references from a recognized bank or law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High inbound receipts from cross-border marketplaces (Amazon, eBay, etc.) without a direct contract to the AG
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Intercompany or marketplace seller agreement with the legal entity CH_AG (not personal names); 2) verified registration in the Swiss commercial register (Handelsregister) with legal form AG; 3) VAT registration confirmation (MWST) and evidence of the effective place of management in Switzerland; 4) reconciliation of transaction volumes with corporate bank statements; 5) documented compliance with Swiss price and consumer protection laws (LGB/CAG), electronic equipment warranty (VBO).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds between corporate account, fintech EMIs, and supplier accounts in Hong Kong or China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Master supply agreement with Chinese/HK electronics suppliers; 2) import chain documentation (pro-forma invoice, bill of lading, commercial invoice) to prove real trade; 3) supplier validation via Dun & Bradstreet or local chamber of commerce; 4) cash-flow model on accelerated payment cycles; 5) AML policy including no cash payments, no third-party settlement, and no pouch trade (cashless / non-trade goods).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial capital of a Swiss AG (CHF 20,000 minimum for AG under Art. 621 OR), wire transfers must come from the shareholder's personal or corporate bank account by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA if CHF/EUR) citing payment purpose code: 'Kapitaleinlage / Einzahlung auf das Aktienkapital' (English: 'Capital contribution / payment towards share capital'). A Swiss bank account can be funded via SEPA credit transfer (European Economic Area) or SWIFT from any jurisdiction. The bank will require a formal copy of the notarised statutes (pubic deed) and the auditor's confirmation of the initial capital (if higher than CHF 20,000, a bank confirmation or the bank itself confirms to the notary). For foreign capital injection, use the bank's FX desk to convert to CHF and ensure the final debit message uses the beneficiary's name exactly matching the corporate charter. Bearer shares are prohibited for newly formed AGs since 2019; therefore, the bank is legally allowed to receive the funds without obtaining endorsement of physical share certificates. All inbound transfers must exclude sanctioned countries and pass beneficial ownership verification before funds are credited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a consumer electronics e-commerce operator, outbound disbursements include (i) supplier payments to wholesale electronics manufacturers in China/HK/Vietnam; (ii) logistics and freight (DHL, FedEx, Swiss Post), (iii) payment processor settlement (Stripe/PayPal), (iv) royalties and service fees, and (v) dividends. Primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 for all foreign-currency wire transfers. For high-value merchandise (>USD 50,000 or equivalent), a commercial documentary letter of credit (L/C at sight) can be issued via UBS or ZKB; for repeat high-volume low-value orders, open account with SWIFT MT103 is suitable. All outgoing payments must use the correct Swiss payment purpose codes (e.g., 'Exportgutschrift' / 'Warenbezug' / 'Lizenzgebühren') and maintain underlying contracts and warehouse receipts. There is no surrender requirement and no export licensing for consumer electronics, except for items falling under Swiss export control (dual-use, cryptographic) — smartphone and personal gadgets generally require no license. SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) is available for euro payments within the EU/EEA; CHF payments use SIC / SIC5 (instant), both operated by SIX Interbank Clearing. For cross-border CHF, SWIFT is mandatory. Use FX forward within the same bank to limit currency exposure before executing MT103.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) on a settled basis – freely permissible without fundamental rights or regulatory restriction; standard ISDA or bank's standard T&Cs. No SNB approval needed.
FX options (European plain vanilla options) on CHF cross-rates, executed via a bank under the Swiss Bankers Association FX master agreement, if bank counterparty credit is acceptable.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between CHF and USD/EUR for longer-term financing or liability management, permitted under Swiss private law with standard ISDA collateral. Subject to prudential margin rules only for covered financial counterparties, not for a retailer.

Non-centrally cleared FX forwards in CHF do not require mandatory margin if terminated within T+2 but are also permissible for longer-dated trades with initial margin under EMIR for a small non-financial counterparty (NFC- below 3 billion EUR threshold) – not a blocker.

Treasury-consistent CNY/CHF spot or forwards via a Swiss bank broker, but NDFs are not applicable because the CNY is not delivered on-shore; for China supplier settlement, the bank may allow a synthetic CNY forward via Offshore CNH (so-called CNH deliverable forward), which is permissible as a deliverable contract.

Pre-approved rolling FX forwards for payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) if the processor supports multi-currency settlement; alternatively, use a multi-currency account with automatic daily sweeps to CHF, which functions as an operational hedge without derivatives.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_clearing_addendum: For same-day CHF liquidity, use SIC5 (instant payment) to settle with counterparties holding a Swiss bank account. For EUR, use SEPA Instant; for USD, use Fedwire or CHIPS (via correspondent bank); for GBP, use Faster Payments. The company should maintain at least two bank relationships (one tier-1 bank + one fintech/e-money institution) to prevent single-point-of-failure in clearing. Minimum target cash position: 10% of monthly revenue in CHF in a domestic operational account, and convertible FX balances curtailed at 2 weeks of expense coverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; no filing with a state agency. The signed statements are retained at the registered office and produced with the annual corporate tax return to the cantonal tax administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM within six months after the balance-sheet date (OR Art. 699). For a 31 December year-end, the AGM must be held no later than 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and hold the AGM exposes board members to criminal liability under OR Art. 325 (fines up to CHF 10,000). Shareholders may obtain a court order compelling the AGM. Persistent non-compliance may lead to administrative dissolution under OR Art. 731b and personal liability for resulting losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent audit report (ordinary audit or limited review) where legally required or when shareholders resolve to commission an audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory auditor (Revisionsstelle) reports to the shareholders; the report is presented to the board and used at the AGM. No copy is filed with the commercial register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the report issued before the AGM. The AGM must be held within six months of the balance-sheet date (OR Art. 699).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a required auditor is a criminal offence under OR Art. 325 (fines up to CHF 10,000); directors may be civilly liable for losses. The AGM cannot validly approve the financial statements if a mandatory audit is absent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register (Handelsregister) update filings for any change in directors, registered office, share capital or articles of association.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual fixed filing date. Each change must be lodged without delay (unverzueglich) after it occurs (OR Art. 934). A standalone annual confirmation is not required under Swiss law.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of a required filing allows the register authority to impose an administrative fine up to CHF 5,000 (OR Art. 943) and to compel the filing. Continued non-compliance may result in compulsory deregistration (OR Art. 732) and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Internal annual verification of the share register (Aktienbuch) and of outstanding beneficial-owner records, performed by the board before the AGM.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing. The registers are kept at the registered office and are available for review by the commercial register authority, tax authorities, law enforcement and financial intermediaries for KYC purposes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no statutory annual date; the share register must be kept continuously current. An annual compliance review is best-practice and is usually completed immediately before the AGM.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate share registers expose directors to criminal liability under OR Art. 325 and to civil claims. For any bearer shares, breach of the beneficial-owner documentation duty can result in fines up to CHF 500,000 under the Swiss Anti-Money-Laundering Act and suspension of voting and dividend rights for non-registered holders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary audit is mandatory when two of three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive years: balance-sheet total of CHF 20 million, annual turnover of CHF 40 million, and 250 full-time employees on annual average. Where no ordinary audit is required, the general meeting may unanimously dispense with all auditing; otherwise a limited review is required if shareholders holding at least 10% of the share capital demand it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 957-960) is the statutory minimum. Swiss GAAP FER and IFRS are recognised as permissible enhanced frameworks; IFRS is compulsory for listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland has no public UBO register and no annual confirmation statement directed to the state. The AG must maintain an internal share register at its registered office. For any outstanding bearer shares (rare after the abolition for non-listed companies), a register of beneficial owners is separately mandated. Before each AGM the board reviews share-transfer postings and UBO data and records that review in the board minutes. The register is not filed annually with the government, but must be made available upon lawful request to the commercial register, prosecutors, tax authorities and financial intermediaries engaged for banking or payment services.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders' and Board Meetings (Protokollbuch)
Accounting books and vouchers (retention period 10 years)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal effective corporate direct tax at 4.25% (gross statutory rate 8.5% on pre-deduction profit); combined with cantonal and communal profit taxes the all-in statutory headline range for a Swiss CH-AG is approximately 11.9% (Canton Zug) to 21.0% (high-tax cantons such as Zurich).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday applies to consumer-electronics retail. Effective relief instruments under the 2020 Swiss Corporate Tax Reform are: (i) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) exempting dividend and capital-gain income from qualifying holdings (10% ownership or CHF 1 million market value, holding period at least one year), (ii) cantonal patent box / license box with up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income subject to a statutory profit cap, (iii) cantonal R&D super-deduction allowing up to 150% of qualifying R&D personnel and contract research costs, (iv) notional interest deduction (NID) on safe-haven excess equity at cantonal option, and (v) cantonal capital-tax relief on equity attributable to qualifying holding interests.
